title: Durability and long-term safety of ketamine for depression
bottleneck: Ketamine and esketamine relieve depressive symptoms within hours, but the effect typically fades within days to weeks, requiring repeated dosing whose long-term cognitive, bladder, and dependence risks are unquantified. No biomarker predicts who sustains response, and maintenance protocols are empirical.
why_it_blocks: Rapid-acting treatment is psychiatry's biggest advance in decades, but without durable, safe maintenance strategies it remains a crisis intervention rather than a cure, accessible mainly to those who can afford repeated clinic visits.
current_state: Esketamine nasal spray is approved for treatment-resistant depression with a REMS monitoring program. Research into next-generation NMDA modulators and psychedelics aims for longer-lasting effects with fewer dissociative side effects. Efforts to extend ketamine's effect with psychotherapy integration or maintenance dosing show promise, but optimal schedules and long-term bladder and cognitive safety are unestablished.
